articles.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
articles.summary: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists. Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”.
body: Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion.

She was one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken critics throughout his rise to power. She labelled him “harasser in chief”, a man whose rhetoric and conduct ran counter to the values she had dedicated her life to advocating.

In 1963, when Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique – describing the frustration of affluent, well-educated, middle-class white women trapped in domesticity – Steinem was “a girl reporter” living in New York, working on The Beach Book, a compendium of extracts from literature about beaches and tips on what to do in the sun. A rising media star who was later described, to her annoyance, as “the world’s most beautiful byline”, she had already begun to make connections: she asked the economist JK Galbraith to write the foreword, and he agreed.
points: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists.

articles.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
articles.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. Around six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.
points: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.
But it’s possible his preference is already clear.

articles.title: A sun goddess, hundreds of devotees – and polluted water: the Nigerian festival threatened by gold mining
articles.summary: Each year, people from across the world gather in a grove sacred to the Yoruba goddess Osun to be healed, conceive or realise their deepest wishes. But toxic lead, mercury and cyanide is leaching into the river.
body: 7Devotees in white clothing line the riverbank, praying as they carry offerings of fruit, kola nut and sacrificial animals in supplication to Osun, the Yoruba goddess of fertility, beauty and healing, whose carved form stands with arms outstretched a few metres away in the Osun River.
It is the final day of Nigeria’s annual Osun Osogbo festival in honour of the African deity, in a tradition that has existed for hundreds of years and draws people from across the diaspora.

Except this year the water was once again a discoloured brown. Until 2018, the river ran clear, but then mining several miles upstream began to pollute it, introducing heavy metals and sediment into the watercourse.

The river, named after the goddess, runs through the Osun-Osogbo sacred grove, a 75-hectare (185-acre) Unesco world heritage site since 2005. The water is believed to possess healing powers and women who have trouble conceiving, or people in search of promotion or prosperity, often come to pray at the riverbank; the water is drunk or used for bathing, depending on the “directions” of the goddess.
points: Each year, people from across the world gather in a grove sacred to the Yoruba goddess Osun to be healed, conceive or realise their deepest wishes.

articles.title: The Best Citrus Perfumes are Surprisingly Versatile
articles.summary: According to experts, citrus pairs beautifully with other notes, making the best citrus fragrances by Dior, Guerlain, and more surprisingly versatile.
body: If fruity fragrances lean too sweet for your liking, and clean scents too minimalist, perhaps the best citrus perfumes are an ideal middle ground. A well-crafted citrus scent doesn’t smell like your average multi-surface home cleaning spray, or just a simple squeeze of lemon—it’s a more nuanced than that.

“A fruity perfume and a citrus-forward perfume speak entirely different languages on the skin,” Guerlain perfume creative director, Delphine Jelk, tells Vogue. “A fruity fragrance is about lushness, roundness, and indulgence and often leans gourmand or soft. Citrus, on the other hand, is about light, energy, and crispness. Citrus notes come from the zests—the peel—so they offer an immediate, sparkling bite, an awakening of the senses.”

articles.title: Kendall Jenner Has Her Own Kind of Romance
articles.summary: The model and face of Emporio Armani’s Power of You fragrance reflects on her first Venice Film Festival and the beauty rituals she learned from her mom.
body: It’s only Kendall Jenner’s second time in the city of Venice —and her first at the Venice Film Festival. When Vogue catches up with her, she has barely had time to settle in: she landed the previous day and will be gone again by morning. First, though, there is a dress to put on and a debut festival carpet to walk.

Venice already comes with its own rather romantic Jenner family association. Her first visit, last summer, was for a wedding, and Kylie Jenner came as her date. “It was just like we were on just a million dates together in Venice,” she remembers. “So I’d say now, Venice reminds me of Kylie, which is really sweet. It’s sisterly romance.” There are, of course, the city’s more obvious charms, too. “It’s so beautiful. It’s so unique. It’s one of a kind.”

Scent, it turns out, is also something Jenner associates with the women in her family. Fragrance is the final consideration in her everyday getting-ready routine. “At the end of getting dressed, I’m like, ‘Who am I today? What scent am I today?’” she says. “I’m a little bit of a snob about it too. I’m super picky about my scents.”
points: The model and face of Emporio Armani’s Power of You fragrance reflects on her first Venice Film Festival and the beauty rituals she learned from her mom.

articles.title: Gloria Steinem’s Best Style Moments
articles.summary: The trailblazing journalist and social movement leader Gloria Steinem has died age 92. Vogue reflects on her style legacy and fashion as rebellion.
body: Gloria Steinem’s most famous—and oft-repeated—quotes naturally concern equality, women’s rights, resistance, and revolution. But the legendary journalist, pioneering feminist, and social movement organizer—who has died at the age of 92 —also had a thing or two to teach us about style.

Despite being criticized in the ’70s by those who felt her glamorous persona was at odds with her feminist ideology—“the miniskirted pinup girl of the intelligentsia,” as the Post reporter Maxine Cheshire dubbed her—Steinem never shied away from fashion. “Fashion in the past meant conforming and losing oneself,” she said in the 2011 documentary Gloria. “Fashion in the present means being unique and finding oneself.”

Alongside her advocacy work, her sense of style was committed to screen with the Hulu series Mrs America, which explored her role in the movement to ratify the Equal Rights Amendment through bell-bottomed, paisley shirt-wearing Rose Byrne playing Steinem. Then there was The Glorias, which saw both Julianne Moore and Alicia Vikander step into Steinem’s flares.
points: The trailblazing journalist and social movement leader Gloria Steinem has died age 92.

articles.title: Is the Cropped Trench Coat the Ultimate Transitional Hero?
articles.summary: From the runways to the high street, cropped trench coats are in for fall—and in a big way. Discover our favorites to streamline your transitional wardrobe.
body: Designers love to reimagine a classic, and for the tricky transitional season, the trench coat is no exception. Creative directors have taken scissors to the staple, cropping inches off its hemline. The result? A boxier shoulder, plenty of legroom, and a fresh silhouette. While we’ve long waxed poetic about the timeless full-length version, its shorter counterpart feels both chicer and sportier than many of its traditional iterations.

From Burberry and Balenciaga to Frame and Cos, cropped trench coats deliver a tailored, cinched-waist silhouette that suits just about everyone. And they’re versatile too: Style them with everything from plain white tees and great denim to lightweight knits and polished midiskirts.

articles.title: A Bunch of AI Platforms Are Down, Including ChatGPT
articles.summary: If you had trouble accessing AI platforms Thursday morning, you're not alone. Apps and services, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok, were down, or experienced issues with service. ChatGPT and Grok were both unresponsive when I tried to use them, while Claude appeared to respond, at least for me.
body: ChatGPT appears to be experiencing the most issues, at least per Downdetector. The site, which accepts user reports of issues with apps and services, currently shows tens of thousands of reports for ChatGPT alone. Claude and Grok had fewer reports, but still many (thousands) over the course of this morning.

According to OpenAI's status page, the company had experienced issues with both ChatGPT and Codex. Anthropic had also acknowledged issues with Claude, including for its Mythos 5.1, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5 models, and said it is working on a fix. SpaceXAI shows that all Grok functions appear to be down at this time. As of 1:19 p.m. ET, all three services now report that they're now up and running.

It's not clear exactly what caused these issues, or if they were all related to one another. Typically, outages like these are solved relatively quickly, so it's not a surprise that all three were able to get their systems back by early afternoon. I'll continue to monitor the situation and update this piece accordingly.
